key_insight: CalTwin combines Fisher-information shift regularisation with a confidence-misalignment penalty to make medical world models more robust to hospital/domain shifts and better calibrated.
clinical_relevance: This could improve the reliability of latent patient-state forecasting for tasks like sepsis monitoring, imaging-based prediction, and digital-twin treatment planning across different clinical sites.
method: GRU-based medical world model with a latent transition predictor
Fisher-Information-based penalty to reduce covariate shift across fragmented training data
Confidence Misalignment Penalty to reduce overconfident multi-step forecasts
evidence_signal: On PhysioNet 2019 Sepsis Challenge data, using two hospital systems for training and a third as OOD test, CalTwin reduced OOD next-step latent-state MSE by 9.1% and slightly improved ECE (0.7%).
watch_item: The calibration gain was small, so practical benefit may depend on whether the added regularisation justifies the extra complexity and whether results generalise beyond the sepsis benchmark.
paper_title: CalTwin: Towards Calibrated, Shift-Robust Medical World Models via Fisher-Information Regularisation
